Abstract  
We investigated the contents of the sequencing study PRJEB1234 by querying the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) via the BRC Analytics ENA portal. Using the brc_ena_study tool with accession PRJEB1234, we retrieved study metadata, a total run count, the organisms represented, and a truncated subset of run records. The query returned that the study “A haplotype map of foxtail millet genome” (secondary accession ERP002070) comprises 916 sequencing runs across two species (Setaria italica and Setaria viridis). Due to size limitations, 28 run entries were returned in this response, but all 916 are available via paging. Understanding these study parameters is essential for researchers planning downstream analyses, such as sample selection, genome assembly, or population genomics studies, by providing precise counts, taxonomic scope, and access to raw FASTQ data.

I. Introduction  
Background. The study PRJEB1234 publishes whole-genome shotgun (WGS) sequencing data for foxtail millet (Setaria italica) and its wild relative (S. viridis). Such a haplotype map underpins genetic diversity and trait mapping research in cereal genomics.  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap. Prior to querying, the exact number of runs, taxonomic breakdown, and metadata details of PRJEB1234 were not programmatically known.  
Objective & Hypothesis. We aimed to characterize PRJEB1234 by retrieving its run count, organism composition, study title, and sample-level metadata, hypothesizing that the study contains hundreds of WGS runs spanning two Setaria species.

II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. We accessed the ENA study-level metadata through BRC Analytics’ federated ENA portal to obtain structured information about PRJEB1234.  
Materials. The brc_ena_study tool was used to query study details from the ENA portal.  
Procedures.  
1. Invoked brc_ena_study with arguments:  
   • study_accession: "PRJEB1234"  
2. No additional filters or paging parameters were applied.  
Statistical Analysis.  
• Total run count (“run_count” field) was taken as the study’s size (denominator = 916).  
• Number of organisms derived from the length of “organisms_in_runs” array (n = 2).  
• Number of run records returned without paging = 28; total matching = 916.

III. Results  
Data Presentation.  
Table 1 summarizes the key metrics returned by the query.  

Table 1. Summary of PRJEB1234 content  
| Metric                              | Value               | Source Field                 |  
|-------------------------------------|---------------------|------------------------------|  
| Study title                         | A haplotype map of foxtail millet genome | study.study_title           |  
| Secondary study accession           | ERP002070           | study.secondary_study_accession |  
| First public date                   | 2013-06-06          | study.first_public          |  
| Total sequencing runs               | 916                 | run_count                   |  
| Organisms represented               | 2                   | organisms_in_runs.length    |  
| Species names                       | Setaria italica; Setaria viridis | organisms_in_runs          |  
| Records returned in this response   | 28                  | size_capped.returned        |  
| Records available (total matching)  | 916                 | size_capped.total_matching  |  

Findings. The study comprises 916 paired-end WGS runs spanning two species. The ENA portal returned 28 run records in this response.

IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. The results confirm that PRJEB1234 is a large-scale WGS project covering two species with nearly one thousand runs, supporting its designation as a comprehensive haplotype map.  
Context. These findings align with the study metadata—title, accession, and publication date—retrieved from the ENA portal and provide an entry point to individual run data (FASTQ URLs).  
Limitations. The JSON response was truncated to 28 records due to character limits; all 916 runs require paging via brc_ena_runs. The study-level tax_id and scientific_name fields were empty.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. PRJEB1234 offers extensive genomic data for Setaria species. Future queries should page through all runs (e.g., with brc_ena_runs by taxonomy_id or offset) or target specific run accessions to retrieve full FASTQ download URLs and sample metadata.

References  
[1] BRC Analytics ENA portal API filereport for study PRJEB1234. URL: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport?accession=PRJEB1234

Acknowledgments  
We acknowledge the European Bioinformatics Institute (EBI) for providing the ENA data and the BRC Analytics portal for federating access.
